title: Counit-normalized etale/pro-etale transport of the finite clopen mate
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $Q$ be a commutative square of schemes with $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ quasi-compact open immersions, $r:V\to S$, $p:W\to T$ proper, and $pk=ir$. Put $W_S=W\times_T S$ with projections $b:W_S\to W$, $q:W_S\to S$, and $s=(k,r):V\to W_S$. Write $A_X=\nu_X^*$ for exact etale/pro-etale comparison on module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Use the canonical bounded-below open comparison [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-site-extension] and the etale clopen transformations and normalized comparison [def-cbc-etale-clopen-mate-normalization-data]. On either site form $\alpha_Q^e,\alpha_Q^p$ by the open-unit cartesian comparison followed by projection to the clopen lift $s(V)$ and the open compositor. Let $\gamma_Q^e,\gamma_Q^p$ be their proper-adjunction mates, and take $\gamma_Q^e$ with the resolution normalization of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. For $u=p,r$, use the pullback comparison $a_u:A_{dom(u)}G_u^e\cong G_u^pA_{cod(u)}$ and the canonical direct-image comparison $b_u:A_{cod(u)}R_u^e\to R_u^pA_{dom(u)}$, satisfying
$$\varepsilon_u^p\circ G_u^p(b_u)\circ a_u=A_{dom(u)}(\varepsilon_u^e).$$
For every $L\in D^+(V_{et},\Lambda)$, both $L$ and $k_!L$ lie in the bounded-below comparison domains, and $p,r$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated with no Noetherian assumption. The canonical open and pullback comparisons identify $A_W\alpha_Q^e$ with $\alpha_Q^p$, including its identity/zero component normalization. Let $o_j:A_{cod(j)}J_j^e\cong J_j^pA_{dom(j)}$ be the adjoint open comparison. Then
$$\gamma^p_{Q,A_VL}\circ J_i^p(b_{r,L})\circ o_{i,R_r^eL}
=R_p^p(o_{k,L})\circ b_{p,J_k^eL}\circ A_T(\gamma^e_{Q,L}).$$
Every comparison in this equation is the specified canonical one. They and $\gamma^e_{Q,L}$ are isomorphisms, so $\gamma^p_{Q,A_VL}$ is an isomorphism with exactly the finite etale proper/open and refinement normalization.

proof.text: Properness makes $p,r$ finite type, hence quasi-compact; their diagonals are closed immersions, so they are quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Exactness of $k_!$ gives $\mathcal H^n(k_!L)=k_!\mathcal H^n(L)$, so any lower bound for $L$ is also one for $k_!L$. The canonical-mate comparison therefore applies to $(u,K)=(r,L)$ and $(p,k_!L)$ and gives exactly the named invertible $b_r,b_p$ and their counit equations. Here finite rings are discrete. No absolute quasi-compactness, finite-dimensionality or Noetherian hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison; apply the existing canonical-mate comparison with its actual qcqs hypotheses

proof.text: Apply lem-cbc-finite-clopen-alpha-site-transport to obtain the displayed equality of the specified alphas on D+. This is the sheaf/compositor/localization part of the original argument, separated from the proper-mate calculation.
Apply the bounded-below clause of etaleClopenMateNormalization to identify the specified etale mate with normalizedComparison, componentwise at L.

Put $X=A_TJ_i^eR_r^eL$ and $Y=J_k^pA_VL$. Transpose the proposed left-hand side, a map $X\to R_p^pY$, under $G_p^p\dashv R_p^p$, and precompose with the isomorphism $a_{p,J_i^eR_r^eL}$. The defining mate identity for $\gamma^p$ and naturality of $\alpha^p$ in $b_{r,L}$ give
$$J_k^p(\varepsilon_r^p\circ G_r^p(b_{r,L}))\circ\alpha^p_{Q,A_SR_r^eL}\circ G_p^p(o_{i,R_r^eL})\circ a_{p,J_i^eR_r^eL}.$$
Substitute step 4 with $M=R_r^eL$, then the normalized counit equation for $r$, and use naturality of $o_k$. The result is
$$o_{k,L}\circ A_W(J_k^e(\varepsilon^e_{r,L})\circ\alpha^e_{Q,R_r^eL}).$$
These substitutions use the natural transformation $b_r$ at $L$, not any inverse chosen from an existence theorem.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; explicit proper-adjunction transpose and counit substitution

proof.text:
Transpose the proposed right-hand side and precompose with the same $a_p$. Naturality of the pro-etale counit first moves $o_{k,L}$ outside the transpose. Naturality of $a_p$ in $\gamma^e_{Q,L}$ and the normalized counit equation for $p$, now at $J_k^eL$, give
$$o_{k,L}\circ A_W(\varepsilon^e_{p,J_k^eL}\circ G_p^e(\gamma^e_{Q,L})).$$
The etale mate identity identifies the parenthesis with $J_k^e(\varepsilon^e_{r,L})\circ\alpha^e_{Q,R_r^eL}$, exactly the expression in step 5. Cancel $a_p$ and use injectivity of the proper adjunction bijection. This proves the displayed equation in the item as an equality of the specified morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; explicit transpose of the other route

proof.text: The maps $o_i,o_k$ are isomorphisms, as are $b_{r,L}$ and $b_{p,J_k^eL}$ by step 1. The normalized etale comparison is an isomorphism by [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so the proved equality expresses $\gamma^p_{Q,A_VL}$ as the composite of the right-hand route with the inverse of $J_i^p(b_{r,L})\circ o_{i,R_r^eL}$. It is therefore an isomorphism. Step 4 identifies the finite etale and refinement normalizations before taking mates, so the resulting isomorphism has exactly those normalizations. Empty opens, empty complements, identity squares and the zero ring are included: the component formula is still $(x,y)\mapsto(x,0)$, with a missing component the zero module.

Steps 1-4 check out. Step 1: properness gives finite type, hence quasi-compactness, and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness via lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated. Exactness of k_! keeps k_!L in D^+, so the canonical-mate comparison gives the invertible b_r, b_p and their counit equations. Step 2: the square (i,p,b,q) is cartesian, so both extension-by-zero base-change nodes apply. The open comparison is defined as the mate of the restriction comparison (lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison step 1, Stacks 09AF), so it respects the open unit, and the pullback comparison respects the cartesian compositor. Step 3: the projection onto the clopen piece is pinned down by binary gluing over W_S = s(V) ⊔ C, first on sheaves, then degreewise, then after localization. Step 4: the transported α equation types correctly. Steps 5-6: I recomputed both transposes symbol by symbol, using naturality of α^p in b_r, the r- and p-counit equations, naturality of a_p and o_k, and the étale mate identity; both reduce to o_{k,L}∘A_W(J_kε^e_r∘α^e). Step 7: the cited comparisons and γ^e are isomorphisms, so γ^p is invertible on objects A_V L. The step rightly does not claim α is invertible. Edge cases checked: empty V or C, the refinement case r=id, identity squares, the zero ring. The off-unit tool_uses (qs lemma, j_! exactness, pullback and canonical direct-image comparisons, mate definition) are generic black boxes and accepted. review_split's 'no such node' messages are an artefact of the symlinked snapshot; I opened every cited node. No duplicate in the DAG: the sf site-transport nodes and the ambient clopen comparison node are pro-étale-internal. Source tags 099R and 09AF are present in Stacks proetale.tex; no SGA. No fixes.
